check3_ambiguous_and_malformed_payload_p.claim_tested: Whether the version-dispatching model_validator ever silently misinterprets an ambiguous or malformed payload as the wrong version, rather than failing loudly.

probes.name: neither exposure_contract_version nor impact_contract_version key present
probes.result: Raises pydantic.ValidationError with an explicit message naming both missing keys. FAILS LOUDLY, correctly. No defect.

probes.name: BOTH exposure_contract_version and impact_contract_version keys present (conflation probe)
probes.result: The v2 branch is checked first (exposure_contract_version wins) and the leftover v1-only keys (impact_contract_version, outcome_name, historical_impact, etc.) are then rejected by ContractModel's extra='forbid' as 'Extra inputs are not permitted' (9 validation errors). FAILS LOUDLY, correctly -- this exact input shape cannot arise from any real producer (validate_candidates.py's v2 dict never carries impact_contract_version), so this is a defensive-depth confirmation, not a live gap.

probes.name: v1-shaped payload missing a required legacy field (own probes: missing 'historical_impact', separately missing 'materiality_pass')
probes.result: normalize_economic_impact_payload does direct dict indexing (data['historical_impact'], data['materiality_pass'], etc.) for several legacy fields. A missing key raises a raw, UNWRAPPED KeyError, not a pydantic.ValidationError -- pydantic's model_validator(mode='before') only auto-wraps ValueError/TypeError/AssertionError into ValidationError, not KeyError, so this propagates as a bare Python exception (a 500 with an opaque stack trace at the live API route, not a clean validation error message) rather than the clean, informative failure the neither-key-present branch produces.
probes.severity: minor -- FINDING, not blocking. Still fails loudly (a hard crash, not a silent misinterpretation or wrong-version reinterpretation) -- the central migration-safety invariant holds -- but the failure mode is inconsistent and less operable/debuggable than the rest of the same function. Only reachable via a genuinely corrupted/truncated legacy DB row, which the real pipeline never produces.

probes.name: v2-shaped payload with tier1=None AND tier2=None but reportable_tiers=[1] (self-contradictory: claims tier 1 reportable while carrying no tier1 data)
probes.result: ACCEPTED without any validation error. No cross-field invariant on EconomicImpactPersistence checks that reportable_tiers only references tiers that are actually populated (contrast: CandidateExposureTierPersistence DOES have such a check for its own annualization fields). impact.outcome_name property then silently returns None rather than raising.
probes.severity: minor -- FINDING, not blocking. This is a same-version internal-consistency gap, not a v1/v2 conflation -- it never causes a payload to be misread as the wrong contract version. Not reachable through the real pipeline: validate_candidates.py always derives reportable_tiers from CandidateValidation.reportable_exposure_tiers(), which is itself derived from the actually-populated tier1/tier2 objects, so reportable_tiers can never legitimately name an unpopulated tier in practice. Only reachable via hand-crafted or corrupted input. Downstream effect if it did occur: app.policies.backtest_service.trigger_backtest would see outcome_name=None, compare != _SUPPORTED_OUTCOME, and return a clean (if slightly misleading) 409 -- not a crash, not silent wrong data exposed to a user.

probes.name: empty-string impact_contract_version
probes.result: Raises pydantic.ValidationError (string_too_short on the nested tier1.exposure_contract_version, min_length=1). FAILS LOUDLY, correctly.

probes.name: garbage dict with unrelated keys, no version markers
probes.result: Raises the same clean 'neither key present' ValidationError. FAILS LOUDLY, correctly.

check3_ambiguous_and_malformed_payload_p.verdict: CONFIRMED overall (no silent v1/v2 conflation found under adversarial construction) -- two minor, non-blocking, non-silent robustness findings disclosed above, neither reachable through the real pipeline.
